name: Carboplatin
route_note: IV infusion, dose usually calculated from renal function (Calvert formula, target AUC)
originator: Institute of Cancer Research and Johnson Matthey (UK); developed by Bristol-Myers

discovery.by: Johnson Matthey and the Institute of Cancer Research (Kenneth Harrap)
discovery.note: A second-generation platinum analogue designed with a cyclobutanedicarboxylate leaving group to reduce cisplatin's kidney toxicity.

tagline: Second-generation platinum drug with less kidney and nerve toxicity than cisplatin
summary: Carboplatin is a platinum analogue that forms the same DNA adducts as cisplatin but reacts more slowly, giving less nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity and nausea at the cost of more bone-marrow suppression. It is a standard drug in ovarian and lung cancer and many combination regimens.
mechanism: The bidentate cyclobutanedicarboxylate ligand is displaced far more slowly than cisplatin's chlorides, so carboplatin is more stable in plasma and is largely excreted unchanged.

Once activated inside cells it forms the same platinum–DNA intrastrand cross-links as cisplatin, blocking replication and inducing apoptosis. Higher doses are needed to achieve equivalent DNA platination.
uses: Head and neck, bladder, cervical, endometrial and breast cancer regimens
Germ-cell tumours and paediatric tumours (e.g. retinoblastoma, neuroblastoma)

history.title: Analogue programme
history.detail: Johnson Matthey and the Institute of Cancer Research synthesise second-generation platinum analogues.

history.title: Clinical trials
history.detail: Phase I studies at the Royal Marsden show reduced renal toxicity compared with cisplatin.

history.title: UK approval
history.detail: Launched in the UK as Paraplatin.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US for advanced ovarian cancer.

history.title: Calvert formula
history.detail: Calvert and colleagues publish AUC-based dosing using glomerular filtration rate.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic carboplatin enters the US market after patent expiry.

pk.half_life: about 2.6–5.9 hours (free platinum) with normal renal function

serious: hypersensitivity reactions, increasing with repeated cycles
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for bone-marrow suppression, vomiting and anaphylactic-like reactions.

facts: Dose by target AUC (Calvert formula: dose = AUC × [GFR + 25]) is a standard pharmacokinetic calculation in oncology.
